newsitem.title: USA: Nike CEO "surprised" by strong business.
newsitem.headline: Nike CEO "surprised" by strong business.

text.p: Nike Inc Chairman and chief executive officer Philip Knight said he was surprised by the company's strong sales and order growth over the past six weeks.
"We had a great quarter and we're very, very pleased with it," Knight told analysts in a conference call after the company reported record second-quarter results.

"It surprised us and I think it surprised a lot of the analysts in terms of where we thought we were going to be as recently as six weeks ago," he said. "It was really a good quarter across the baord."
Nike President and chief operating officer Tom Clarke said his recent discussions with retailers indicated the current holiday season would be a strong one.
"Almost to a retailer, people are feeling very good about how sales are going thorugh the holiday period," he said. "We like the way the holiday season is shaping up."

He said countries outside the United States continued to show the fastest growth and forecast that around the year 2000 international markets would represent 50 percent of the company's revenues, up from about 39 percent currently.

Clarke and others particularly highlighted Japan, now the company's largest market outside the United States with revenues in the quarter up 199 percent over the year-earlier period on a constant-dollar basis. Executives did not give a specific figure.
"What we're striving to do is become the local sports brand of choice in Japan," Clarke said.
Chief financial officer Robert Falcone said the company's gross margin for the fiscal year to date was 39.9 percent of sales, up from 39.8 percent in the comparable year-earlier period.
He said "there may be a little slippage", but expected margins to hold steady through the end of the fiscal year in May. "I wouldn't look to forecast any growth from where we are now," he said.
He said the company remained on target to hold selling, general and administrative expenses to under 25 percent of sales for the year as it did last year.
